subject: Service credit request — CalderaHealth (12 Jun 2027 incident, billing reconciliation)
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@calderahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: CalderaHealth Billing <billing@calderahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Service credit request — CalderaHealth (12 Jun 2027 incident)

Hi Soojin,

Following up from our support thread: on 12 Jun 2027 we experienced a significant service degradation for inference endpoints in us-west-2 between ~01:20 UTC and ~05:40 UTC (intermittent timeouts and retries; final restoration at 05:40). Our internal logs show ~260 minutes of effectively unavailable capacity for production workloads during that window.

Per our SLA (99.95% uptime target) we want to submit a formal service credit request for that billing period. Our June invoice is $21,500 — please advise the calculation you will use, whether this is eligible under the SLA, and how you intend to apply the credit (credit note vs invoice adjustment).

I've attached our uptime report and the signed claim form. Please let us know if you need anything else to process this.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Sr. Platform Engineer
CalderaHealth

Attachments: uptime_report_2027-06-01_06-30.csv, SLA_claim_form_CalderaHealth.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@calderahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, CalderaHealth Billing <billing@calderahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service credit request — CalderaHealth (12 Jun 2027 incident)

Alex — thanks for the detailed packet and the claim form. We're reviewing the ops postmortem and our internal telemetry now. I've looped in Ben from Billing to prepare a quantitative calculation and Marissa from Finance for approvals.

We should have a draft credit amount and proposed application (credit note vs direct invoice adjustment) by end of day tomorrow. Will confirm next steps and timeline for issuance.

Appreciate the patience and sorry for the disruption — we'll make this straightforward.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft credit calculation for CalderaHealth (June billing period)

Team — I ran the numbers with the uptime evidence Alex provided and our postmortem timeline. Inputs:
- Billing period: June 2027 (30 days = 43,200 minutes)
- Recorded unavailable minutes (per Caldera logs & our telemetry): 260 minutes
- Monthly spend per invoice: $21,500
- SLA: 99.95% uptime target; credit calculation = (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_period) * monthly_charge (per SLA table); credit cap = 10% of monthly charge (standard clause)

Calculation: 260 / 43,200 = 0.0060185; 0.0060185 * $21,500 = $129.40
Rounded: $129.40 (below the 10% cap of $2,150).

Eligibility notes: incident is within scope (hosted API region outage), customer provided signed claim form and telemetry match our incident window. No configuration or customer-side mitigation steps that would void the claim were evident.

Proposed route: issue a credit memo for $129.40 applied to the July billing run as an invoice-level credit. I will prepare a credit memo draft and attach it to a DocuSign acknowledgement for CalderaHealth to sign (recordkeeping + audit trail).

If approved, I recommend we also include the ops_postmortem_2027-06-12.pdf link and the JIRA reference in the credit memo.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Best regards,
